Hi mate, thanks for your reply.

I'm going to carry on posting but I might take a little break to gather what I know. I think I've got the idea when it comes to decisions. For instance, in the diagram in the last post, lets assume A came back and consumed all of the orders in B, we would then have a mini compression PAZ. we would be well within our rights to take a trade at A but we would have to have our stop below B. In essence, this is when the FTR in A is at it's strongest, because it has consumed the orders in the FL below, it then becomes the last line of defense, this doesn't mean a reaction is going to take the price in to space, but we should get a reaction at least, to the last decision.

We get in to confusing territory when multiple decisions have not been revisited and they are stacked, I believe this to be a PAZ as well but I'm unsure how to approach it. What I mean by this is every decision is reacting to a decision, If the first decision that started the ball rolling hasn't been consumed we have to expect price to get back there. This is very hard to explain, but think of a small decision, this decison decides to engulf something, the FTB to this decision forms a flag, this flag is then a decision to engulf something else, the FTB to this Flag then forms a flag, if the momentum leaving the flag continues in the same direction again and engulfs something else, we have another decision

It's CP if it's consumed the last orders in each decision, I believe it's stacked demand if it hasn't, either way, from what I've seen they both work in a similar way.

Hope that makes sense,

سلام رفیق، ممنون برای جوابت.

می‌خوام به پست کردن ادامه بدم، ولی شاید کمی وقفه بگیرم تا جمع کنم آنچه می‌دونم رو. فکر می‌کنم وقتی پای decision‌ها میاد ایده رو گرفتم. مثلاً، در diagram پست قبل، فرض کن A برگشت و همهٔ سفارش‌های B رو مصرف کرد؛ اون‌وقت یه فشردگی PAZ کوچیک داشتیم. حق داشتیم توی A معامله بگیریم، ولی استاپمون باید زیر B می‌بود. در essence، این وقتیه که FTR توی A در قوی‌ترین حالته، چون سفارش‌های FL پایین رو مصرف کرده و بعد آخرین خط دفاع می‌شه؛ این به این معنا نیست که reaction قیمت رو به space می‌بره، ولی باید حداقل به آخرین decision reaction بگیریم.

وقتی چند decision revisit نشده و روی‌هم انباشته شدن، وارد سرزمین گیج‌کننده‌ای می‌شیم؛ فکر می‌کنم این هم PAZ هست ولی مطمئن نیستم چطور باید بهش نزدیک بشم. منظوری که دارم اینه که هر decision به decision دیگه‌ای واکنش نشون می‌ده؛ اگه decision اولی که توپ رو به راه انداخت مصرف نشده باشه، باید انتظار داشته باشیم قیمت برگرده اونجا. توضیحش خیلی سخته، ولی یه decision کوچیک رو فکر کن: این decision تصمیم می‌گیره چیزی رو اینگالف کنه، FTB به این decision یه فلگ می‌سازه، این فلگ بعد یه decision برای اینگالف چیز دیگه‌ای می‌شه، FTB به این فلگ بعد یه فلگ دیگه می‌سازه؛ اگه شتاب خروج از فلگ دوباره توی همون جهت ادامه بده و چیز دیگه‌ای رو اینگالف کنه، decision دیگه‌ای داریم.

وقتی CP هست یعنی آخرین سفارش‌ها رو توی هر decision مصرف کرده؛ فکر می‌کنم اگه نکرده باشه stacked تقاضاست؛ به هر حال، از آنچه دیده‌ام هر دو به یه روش مشابه کار می‌کنن.

امیدوارم مفهوم باشه،

couple of things running through my mind, thought I'd post them before i head off for the day. The first is this diagram I've just made. I've bee very focused on DBD's and RBRs recently, Decisions and momentum = orders to me. This diagram lit a light bulb in my head as I was drawing it.

Also, On flag limits, I need to remember scale, I was doing well when I was drawing in clear defined RBR's and DBD's leaving flags. Maybe concentrating on these key areas of buying and selling and only trading the exits from them is where I need to be. Also, something else which is key, within every FL there is a FL and within that FL, there is a FL, every decision has a decision within it.

Patterns are a consequence of decisions, don't trade the patterns, look for the decisions as although it may seem something is reacting of a level in the past, it's actually reacting of a decision that was made last time price was at that level.

Have a good weekend everyone.

Robbie

Edit: I'd like to add that there are different variations of this, like when price FLAGS at the top or bottom for a while.

posts.t:
The flag limit is the feature which defines the flag. As Robbie stated previously, where the flag goes to beyond the limit is not relevant. (Well, it is relevant in so much as where the areas of S/D are within the flag - as this is where price will react on return, once the flag limit is broken.

So, the diagram you've posted above does not show the flag limit, it shows where the flag was (maybe) broken. The full story would be something like I've marked here, where the blue box is the flag limit, defined by the points noted in the green circles ( the FL as the abbreviation). So, what's marked as B is the Decision Point (DP) to break the flag and A is the FTR created after that break.

What I see is that the FTR was the price point the ITs used to be aiming for in the past, and would FO to the DP (B) but nowadays, they aim for B, and what was once the FO zone, has become the new target.
posts.fa:
FL ویژگی‌ایه که فلگ رو تعریف می‌کنه. مثل چیزی که Robbie قبلاً گفت، اینکه فلگ فراتر از limit کجا می‌ره relevant نیست. (خب، تا حدی relevant هست که نواحی عرضه/تقاضا توی فلگ کجان - چون همین‌جاست که قیمت هنگام برگشت واکنش نشون می‌ده، وقتی limit فلگ شکسته بشه.

پس diagram‌ی که بالای پست کردی limit فلگ رو نشون نمی‌ده، نشون می‌ده فلگ کجا (شاید) شکسته شده بود. داستان کامل چیزی شبیه اون چیزیه که اینجا علامت زدم؛ مستطیل آبی limit فلگه، تعریف‌شده با نقاطی که توی دایره‌های سبز نوشتم (FL به‌عنوان abbreviation). پس چیزی که به‌عنوان B علامت خورده Decision Point (DP) برای شکستن فلگه و A هم FTR ساخته‌شده بعد از اون شکسته.

چیزی که می‌بینم اینه که FTR نقطه قیمتی بود که IT‌ها توی گذشته aim کردن بهش و به DP (B) FO می‌کردن، ولی این روزها اونا برای B aim می‌کنن، و اون چیزی که زمانی ناحیه FO بود تارگت جدید شده.

posts.t: Referring # 182 of RCMAF, A question here,are bith A and B tradable and which one is preferred,why?
posts.fa: اشاره به # 182 مربوط به RCMAF، یه سؤال اینجا: آیا هر دو A و B tradeable هستن و کدوم ترجیح داده می‌شه، چرا؟

posts.t:
Harsh, I don't often like to think about "why" as that can sometimes lead to curve fitting.

In the case of A and B, yes, they are both tradeable. A is an FTR, and so I don't think I need explain why or how that is a good place to enter. B is the DP to break the flag limit, and as such is a very important decision. In recent times, this DP has taken on more significance. It used to be the FO area for the FTR, but I beleive that nowaday it has taken on more significance than that.

So, to trade around these areas one MUST consider LTF price action, as price may turn at either A or B, and we want to determine which as best we can. It is good practice to look inside A and B on the LTFs for the significant areas of S and D within.
posts.fa:
Harsh، من اغلب دوست ندارم دربارهٔ "why" فکر کنم چون گاهی می‌تونه به curve fitting منجر بشه.

در مورد A و B، بله، هر دو tradeable هستن. A یه FTR هست، پس فکر نمی‌کنم لازم باشه توضیح بدم چرا یا چطور جای خوبی برای وروده. B همون DP برای شکستن FL‌ه و به‌عنوان اون decision خیلی مهمیه. توی زمان‌های اخیر این DP significance بیشتری گرفته. زمانی ناحیه FO برای FTR بود، ولی فکر می‌کنم این روزها significance بیشتری از اون گرفته.

posts.t:
Cheers, for all of the discussion last week everyone, it was really good, it's important to question each other, it means we have to justify our views not only to other people but ourselves, it's probably the best thing we can do to really learn, not only testing the way we see the market as an individual but also the way our peers see it.

I still have issues with the ambiguity of a certain concept but I can work around that for now. I'm identifying the decision, regardless of what it's called, and to me a decision is supply or demand, it's where the orders are, unless we can be pretty certain the orders have been removed from a decision we must always respect it as a place price want's to go back to.

I took these trades not long ago based on decisions. I've massively reduced my risk while I build confidence, with even 1% risk I would have been quite comfortably done for the day from these three trades. To me my exit was definite pips, this is why I took subsequent shorts upon return to local supply on the way down.

The entry at the top was the only real risk, my first stop had to go above the FO just to be sure. I kept the stops on the next two trades very tight, right above the decisions to the left of the entries.
posts.fa:
ممنون، برای همهٔ بحث‌های هفتهٔ گذشته همه، واقعاً خوب بود؛ مهمه که به هم question بزنیم، یعنی باید view‌هامون رو نه فقط به دیگران بلکه به خودمون justify کنیم. احتمالاً بهترین کاریه که می‌تونیم برای واقعاً یاد گرفتن انجام بدیم؛ نه فقط تست کردن روشی که بازار رو به‌عنوان یه فرد می‌بینیم، بلکه روشی که peers مون می‌بینن.

هنوز با ambiguity مربوط به concept معینی مشکل دارم ولی فعلاً می‌تونم دورش بزنم. decision رو شناسایی می‌کنم، بدون توجه به اینکه چی نامیده می‌شه؛ و برای من decision عرضه یا تقاضاست، جایی که سفارش‌ها هستن، مگر اینکه بتونیم خیلی مطمئن باشیم سفارش‌ها از یه decision برداشته شدن، باید همیشه به اون احترام بذاریم به‌عنوان جایی که قیمت می‌خواد برگرده.

این معامله‌ها رو نه خیلی پیش بر اساس decision‌ها گرفتم. ریسکم رو به‌شدت کم کردم در حالی که دارم confidence می‌سازم؛ حتی با ریسک 1% از این سه معامله برای روز کاملاً راحت done می‌شدم. برای من خروج definite پیپ بود؛ برای همین شورتهای بعدی رو بر اساس برگشت به عرضهٔ محلی توی راه پایین گرفتم.

ورود توی top تنها ریسک واقعی بود؛ استاپ اولم فقط برای اطمینان بالای FO رفت. استاپهای دو معاملهٔ بعدی رو خیلی tight نگه داشتم، درست بالای decision‌های سمت چپ ورودها.

posts.t:
yes mate, there is more than meets the eye, if we can track the important decisions through price they allow us to build up some kind of forward structure depending on what the decision is. What becomes hard is that the fakeout isn't a fakeout anymore, it's where price wants to go in the first place.

Essentially, by convention, we would have to say that price turned at a FL, I think the name is very misleading and that's what causes problems, we then look for structure based upon an ambiguous rules for defining the 'limits' of a flag.

I've set my self on a course to just train my eyes to find the decisions made on price now, as soons as the sequence in the relevant scale of DBD's and RBR's changes, I'm interested if it's somewhere I think a decision on price has been made in the grand scheme of things. Your green lines show this perfectly. I find it's also more helpful to think of DBD's and RBR's for what they actually are, something we are told even in markepedia, supply pole supply, pole and demand pole demand, pole.

I'm guilty of writing off the FTR, I've came around a bit over the weekend, it's tough because many decisions to engulf are also FTR's as well. I think bigger FTR's are good to watch price on a lower TF aslong as we include the decsion above.

As per IF's webinar, If the FTR has FO'd up to the important decision while it's being created, we can expect a QM level from that, what is import though is looking for the actual decision mde the last time price was at that level, where did price decide to FO? and where did it decide that decision it was not longer valid?

I've gone off track, he's a chart with loads of lines on ha.
posts.fa:
بله رفیق، بیشتر از اون چیزیه که چشم می‌بینه؛ اگه بتونیم decision‌های مهم رو از طریق قیمت track کنیم، به ما اجازه می‌دن نوعی forward structure بسازیم، بستگی داره decision چی باشه. چیزی که سخت می‌شه اینه که fakeout دیگه fakeout نیست، جاییه که قیمت از اول می‌خواسته بره.

Essentially، با convention باید بگیم قیمت توی یه FL چرخید؛ فکر می‌کنم اسم خیلی misleading‌ه و برای همین مشکل ایجاد می‌کنه، بعد دنبال structure می‌گردیم بر اساس قواعد ambiguous برای تعریف 'limits' فلگ.

خودم رو روی مسیری گذاشتم که فقط چشم‌هام رو train کنم تا decision‌های گرفته‌شده روی قیمت رو الان پیدا کنه؛ به محض اینکه sequence توی scale مربوط DBD‌های relevant و RBR‌ها تغییر می‌کنه، اگه جایی باشه که فکر می‌کنم decision‌ی روی قیمت توی grand scheme of things گرفته شده، علاقه‌مندم. خط‌های سبز تو این رو کامل نشون می‌دن. می‌فهمم فکر کردن به DBD‌ها و RBR‌ها برای اون چیزی که واقعاً هستن هم کمک‌کننده‌تره — چیزی که حتی توی markepedia به ما می‌گن: عرضه دکل عرضه، دکل و تقاضا دکل تقاضا، دکل.

گناهکارم که FTR رو write off کردم؛ آخر هفته کمی برگشتم سراغش. سخته چون خیلی decision‌های اینگالف هم FTR هستن. فکر می‌کنم FTR‌های بزرگ‌تر برای نگاه به قیمت روی TF پایین خوبن، تا وقتی decision بالایی رو هم بگنجونیم.

طبق webinar مربوط به IF، اگه FTR در حین ساخته شدنش تا decision مهم FO کرده باشه، می‌تونیم QM level‌ی از اون انتظار داشته باشیم؛ اما مهم اینه که decision واقعی گرفته‌شده آخرین بار که قیمت اون سطح بود رو پیدا کنی: قیمت کجا تصمیم گرفت FO کنه؟ و کجا تصمیم گرفت decision دیگه valid نیست؟

از track خارج شدم؛ اینجا چارتی با کلی خط روش ha.
